lastCompletedStory.title: Stop the orchestrator-exit wrapper deleting the live state file

nextStoryContext: buildOrchestratorPaneCommand's teardown ("else", clean-/exit or respawn-cap) branch no longer does `rm -f ${q(opts.stateFile)}`; only readyMarker and pidMarker are still removed there, in the same order as before. `OrchestratorPaneCommandOptions.stateFile` remains a required field on the interface (other call sites still build/pass it) even though the wrapper body no longer reads `opts.stateFile` anywhere -- this is intentional retained shape, not dead code, so do not delete the field or its callers' `stateFile:` properties as a followup cleanup. `cam stop` (performStop, stop.ts) is now the ONLY code path that ever removes cam-loop.local.md; this asymmetry (recycle/exit preserves, explicit stop removes) is the fix, not a bug to unify further. Existing run.test.ts assertions were updated: the old 'removes the loop state file on teardown' test now asserts NOT-containing that rm, and the pidMarker-ordering test was rebased to assert ordering relative to the readyMarker rm instead of the now-removed stateFile rm. A new integration test (test/integration/orch-exit-preserves-state.test.ts) proves this end-to-end via a real bash -c run of the wrapper string with a fake `claude` on PATH that exits 0 with no handoff file (forces the teardown branch on the first loop iteration, no tmux session or polling needed); reuse this fake-claude-exits-immediately pattern for any future test that needs to drive the wrapper's teardown branch deterministically without tmux. US-001 (previous story, same PRD/CAM-195) fixed the FIRST half of Defect 3 (renderStateFile/clearActive phase-collapse); this story (US-002) fixed the SECOND half (the exit wrapper's direct rm). Both halves of Defect 3 are now closed as of this story; if any further story in this PRD references 'Defect 3' it should be treated as fully resolved rather than partially resolved.
